There was either no or poor documentation of other professionals entering the ward and evaluating patients, and the outcome of such assessments not being recorded. 2) Furthermore, during the course of the resuscitation a decision was made for Mr Quinton to be given 4 mgs of Noradreneline. This was to be given as an infusion. Unfortunately, this was actually given as a 4 mg iv bolus. Although the records suggest this did not have a detrimental effect on Mr Quinton (his blood pressure had been exceptionally low) this clearly could be highly significant for other patients. It also raises the question of other patients being given either the wrong drug or the
wrong drug or wrong amount or wrong method of administration
